reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown read Revelation's first-and-last title as Christ knowingly claiming Isaiah's own description of YHWH's eternity, not a rival deity's title.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999-present; print ed. 2013).

sides.snippet: I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.
sides.verseText: Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.

sides.snippet: Don't be afraid. I am the first and the last,
sides.verseText: When I saw him, I fell at his feet like a dead man. He laid his right hand on me, saying, \"Don't be afraid. I am the first and the last,
